items.title: Motion to table an interim control by-law on data centres
items.issue: Council directed staff to draft an interim control by-law pausing new AI data-centre approvals while the city studies land-use, energy, and water impacts. Sponsor: Coun. Nrinder Nann. The actual by-law was scheduled to come back July 15.
items.why: This was the first-reading style vote — it told staff to write the pause, it did not enact it. Hamilton later reversed course at the July 15 sitting.
items.result: Carried 15–1 to draft the ICBL. Coun. Brad Clark was the only councillor reported as voting against. Final by-law vote set for July 15.
items.origin: From June 24, 2026 City Council coverage. Official agenda is on Hamilton’s eScribe portal.

items.title: Interim control by-law on data centres — final vote
items.issue: Council voted on bill 26-127 / CS26006, the by-law that would have paused new AI data-centre approvals in industrial zones. Between June 24 and this sitting, council took a closed legal session; residents described a last-minute briefing that appeared to centre developer and legal risk arguments.
items.why: A pause at the municipal level is one of the few tools communities have while provincial grid-connection rules (Bill 40) are still undefined. Hamilton had a chance to be first in Canada and reversed.
items.result: Defeated 10–6. In favour: Kroetsch, Nann, Francis, Jackson, Pauls, A. Wilson. Opposed: Mayor Horwath, M. Wilson, Hwang, Cooper, Clark, Beattie, Tadeson, Cassar, Spadafora, McMeekin. This reversed the June 24 15–1 direction to draft the by-law.
items.origin: From the July 15, 2026 City Council agenda and recorded-vote coverage.

items.title: Motion to table an interim control by-law on data centres
items.issue: Coun. Martin Reid (Ward 9), seconded by Coun. Sue McFadden, moved that staff prepare an ICBL pausing major digital infrastructure / AI data-centre approvals for up to one year and study Official Plan and zoning rules. Prologis’s Meadowvale proposal was the live file in Ward 9.
items.why: This is the table-the-by-law vote, not the by-law itself. The pause only takes effect if Council adopts the ICBL on September 16.
items.result: Carried unanimously among voting members. Mayor Carolyn Parrish did not cast a vote (Mississauga’s mayor votes only to break a tie) and warned an ICBL would likely be appealed. Final vote: September 16, 2026.
items.origin: From the July 29, 2026 Council agenda and the City’s own news release.

items.title: Final vote on the data-centre interim control by-law
items.issue: Staff bring back the ICBL that Council directed on July 29. If it passes, new data-centre / major digital-infrastructure approvals pause for up to one year while the city studies land use, power, and water. Prologis Meadowvale is the live application. Watch Mayor Parrish — she did not vote in July and has signalled concern about an appeal.
items.why: This is the sitting that either enacts the pause or repeats Hamilton: a strong first vote, then a loss on the actual by-law.

participate.notes: Register a deputation with the Clerk before the agenda deadline. July 29 already had hours of delegations — September 16 is the vote that counts.

items.origin: Based on the official September 16 Council calendar row. City news release set this date for ICBL approval.

items.title: Prologis Meadowvale data-centre-ready campus — ongoing
items.issue: Prologis Meadowvale (Tenth Line West / Argentia, Ward 9) is a proposed ~229,000 sq ft data-centre-ready campus. Residents have pushed for disclosure on water, power, and the unnamed operator. The July 29 ICBL motion was aimed at this file; the pause is not in force until the September 16 vote.
items.why: Site-plan / zoning language written for generic employment land can green-light hyperscale loads without a public hearing framed as a data centre.

participate.notes: Not one sitting — the live vote is September 16 Council. Register a deputation with the Clerk before the agenda deadline.

items.origin: From news coverage. It will not appear as its own row on Mississauga’s calendar until staff put Prologis or the ICBL on an agenda.

items.title: Mayoral direction and motion to table a data-centre ICBL
items.issue: Council received a staff memo on data-centre infrastructure, environment, and planning issues, following a July 21 mayoral direction. Councillors treated it as urgent and directed a special sitting the next day to pass the by-law.
items.why: Oakville had no formal application on file, but industry interest (including a large AI facility discussion) was enough for Council to move in 24 hours.
items.result: Carried unanimously to table / proceed with an ICBL as an urgent matter. Special Council set for August 11 to pass the by-law.
items.origin: Based on the official August 10 Council agenda (item 13.4 Mayoral Direction – Data Centres).

items.title: Interim control by-law on data centres — passed
items.issue: Special Council passed an ICBL under s. 38 of the Planning Act prohibiting new data centres, enterprise computing facilities, and similar high-intensity digital processing for one year (extendable to two) while staff study Official Plan and zoning rules.
items.why: This is the first Ontario municipality to actually pass a data-centre ICBL — Mississauga has only directed staff to write one, and Hamilton defeated theirs.
items.result: Carried unanimously. Oakville is the first town in Ontario to enact a data-centre ICBL. In effect immediately for one year.
items.origin: Based on the official August 11 Special Council agenda and the Town’s August 11 news release.

items.title: Motion for a data-centre interim control by-law — withdrawn
items.location: Council Chambers, Sault Ste. Marie City Hall
items.issue: Ward 3 Coun. Angela Caputo and Ward 2 Coun. Lisa Vezeau-Allen brought an ICBL / moratorium on new data-centre proposals until the city had a policy. After more than an hour of debate the motion was withdrawn. Staff and the mayor argued rezoning already lets Council turn down a bad fit; later in the sitting it was acknowledged the city has had a proposal / inquiries, including hyperscale interest, and the Protexxa project on Yates Avenue is already approved.
items.why: Withdrawing the pause while saying hyperscale ‘wouldn’t fit anyway’ — then confirming a proposal exists — leaves the next sitting as the chance to put a framework or a real freeze on the record.
items.result: Motion withdrawn before a recorded vote. A simplified motion directing staff to write a data-centre framework is expected August 31. No ICBL in force.
items.origin: From the August 10, 2026 Council meeting and news coverage. Official packages are on saultstemarie.ca.

items.title: Follow-up motion — data-centre planning framework
items.location: Council Chambers, Sault Ste. Marie City Hall
items.issue: After withdrawing the ICBL on August 10, sponsors said they would bring a simplified motion directing staff to develop a municipal data-centre framework, with public consultation. This is the sitting to watch if the pause comes back or if Council only studies process.
items.why: A framework without a freeze can still let a live proposal move. Residents are pushing for an education session and a revisit of the ICBL.

participate.notes: Confirm the agenda when the Clerk posts it. Register to speak if the data-centre item is on.

items.origin: From August 10 coverage that flagged August 31 as the next Council date for a rewritten motion.

items.title: Motion to study regional data-centre infrastructure impacts
items.issue: A motion asked York Region to study whether combined data-centre electricity and water demand — plus housing and other industry — exceeds planned supply, because lower-tier cities approve facilities independently.
items.why: Vaughan, Markham, and Richmond Hill can each approve projects the others never see. A regional study is how you catch stacked grid and water load.
items.result: See Regional Council minutes / coverage for the recorded vote.
items.origin: From Richmond Hill’s July 8 motion and news coverage. Official York agendas live on the Region’s meeting portal.
